description.p: Connect to and control your other computers, or let someone help you with theirs, through a server you run yourself. Sessions are encrypted end to end: the server only passes on data it cannot read.

ul.li: Remote control with keyboard and mouse, on X11 and Wayland
Shared clipboard and file transfers in both directions
Direct peer-to-peer connections, relayed by your server when that's not possible
Unattended access to your own devices, and trusted contacts
Identity fingerprints to rule out interception

description.p: SomeDesk needs a SomeDesk server. On Wayland, the desktop asks for permission to share the screen the first time someone connects.

screenshot.caption: The home screen, with this computer's ID and your devices
Accepting a connection, after comparing fingerprints

description.p: Organisations a server can't take over, and servers that hold up against abuse.

ul.li: An organisation's key is shared by its admins, signed, and remembered by their accounts: a server can neither swap it nor hand out older rules
Removing an admin replaces the organisation's key; enrolled machines switch to the new one by themselves
Rules name machines by their keys, not by IDs the server assigns
A device taken off an account no longer reaches the organisation's machines
Being added to an organisation is an invitation you can join or decline
Servers with accounts only take new accounts with an invite code, and limit wrong passwords, connections and relayed traffic per client

description.p: This version is not compatible with 0.2.0: update the app on every device, and the server. Organisations created with 0.2.0 can't be carried over; create them again and re-enroll their machines.
New ways to connect, and optional accounts. Every feature stays free.

ul.li: Unattended access with a password and a code from an authenticator app, checked by the host itself
Optional accounts with two-factor authentication, to reach your own devices and keep an encrypted address book
Organisations: shared access rules, signed by the organisation's admins, and enrollment keys for unattended machines
Device IDs are now bound to a key that stays on the device
Saved passwords in the system keychain, a tray icon, and a single running instance
Remote control on Hyprland, Sway and other wlroots desktops

description.p: This version is not compatible with 0.1.0. Update the app on every device, and update self-hosted servers.
